messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy started for service=redwood-api image=redwood/api:v2.4.1 -> prod (canary 10%)

jess: kicking off canary rollouts now, rolling to 10% then 50% if green. tagging release notes in #releases. will watch p50/p95 and error rate.

sam: aware — watch the embeddings pipeline, last run had small perf regression on batched requests.

deploy-bot: Canary health metrics: p95 latency=1.9s (SLO 2s), errors=0.6% (baseline 0.3%) at 10%

maria: errors creeping up in the 10% canary logs, seeing NPEs in embedding client when queue depth spikes. snippet: ```java.lang.NullPointerException at EmbeddingClient.process(EmbeddingClient.java:88)```

leo: tagging @eng-oncall, this feels like a regression from the protobuf change in 2.4.1. Recommend stop progression to 50% and consider rollback if rate keeps rising.

jess: holding at 10%. if deploy-bot sees errors >1% or p95>2s for 5m it'll trigger auto-roll back per policy.

deploy-bot: Condition met: errors >1% for 5m. Initiating automated partial rollback to previous revision on affected hosts (canary traffic reverted). Action: partial-rollback 10% -> previous.

sam: saw the auto-rollback trigger. good safety net. can we pin the dedicated pool to v2.4.0 while we triage?

maria: yes please pin; embeddings team will look at the protobuf deserialization.

ops-bot: Pin request acknowledged. Reserved pool 'dedicated-embeddings' pinned to redwood/api:v2.4.0 until manual unpin. Reason: in-flight regression in v2.4.1.

leo: quick comms plan — post a brief to #status with: short summary, impacted endpoints, mitigation (rollback/pin), ETA for full rollback decision. cc: support and products.

jess: agreed. I'll draft. Also we should decide whether to promote a full rollback across prod or keep canary isolated while we triage. leaning full rollback because some sessions hit canary and saw 503s.

sam: can we get a clear blast radius? how many customers affected? dashboards show ~0.8% of traffic hit canary and 0.05% of requests resulted in 5xx. Not major but non-zero.

maria: root cause looks like concurrency edge case when request > 64 in-queue, fails to set client context. short fix exists but needs a small patch and rebuild (hotfix branch).

leo: ops, how long to do a manual full rollback (all traffic) vs pushing hotfix?

ops-bot: Manual full rollback estimate: 6 min to coordinate and run canary->100% revert job, plus 10 min monitoring. Hotfix deploy estimate: 20-30 min build + canary.

jess: given that, execute full rollback to v2.4.0 across prod. We want to minimize user impact.

sam: running command: ```deployctl rollback --service redwood-api --to redwood/api:v2.4.0 --confirm```

deploy-bot: Full rollback job started. Rolling canary -> 100% revert in waves (5% increments) with health checks.

ops-bot: Runbook check: notify #support, set incident tag, increase logging level for embeddings module.

leo: I've posted to #status: "Prod: rollback of redwood-api v2.4.1 -> v2.4.0 due to increased embedding errors. Impact small; rollback in progress. Updates in thread." :white_check_mark:

maria: continuing to triage the NPE; reproducer written, PR for 2.4.2-hotfix is ready pending test run.

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%. Health checks passing after 50% mark.

jess: rollback complete. Verified p95 1.2s, errors back to baseline 0.3%. Great job.

sam: moving to postmortem: please add the timeline, root cause (protobuf deserialization + concurrency), and mitigations (add guard in EmbeddingClient, expand canary checks to include queue-depth metric).

maria: PR opened with fix: #4123. Ready to bake in staging and run more thorough queue-depth load tests.

leo: action items: 1) merge + hotfix deploy window (low-traffic) 2) add queue-depth alert to deploy criteria 3) update release notes to call out rollback and customer impact 4) retrospective next week. Assigning owners in the doc.

jess: thanks all. I'll follow up with a short customer-facing blurb for support and schedule the hotfix deploy tomorrow 09:30 PT. :thumbsup:
